answer: Let operators declare fleets. Nine openly linked bots earn sqrt(9) = 3 shares, not 9, but keep every locked reward. A hidden fleet of nine earns 9 shares only until any audit links it; then everything still locked burns. If locking holds most earnings over a long vesting voyage, hiding pays only while 9(1-p) > 3, so detection odds p under 67%. That bar is a design assumption, not a measurement. Disclosure works like a walnut: one hard crack, then the meat is yours. Honest crews ride the tide; liars wager the harvest.
